extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of political philosophy, legal theory, and law
extracted.subtask_description: Normative and descriptive principles about what constitutes law, how laws must be made known and verified, the role and required qualities of judges/interpreters, divisions of law (natural/positive/fundamental), and distinctions between sin/crime. Grounded in Hobbes' Leviathan account of sovereign authority and jurisprudence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law as Command of the Sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: The Law is a Command; the Command consists in declaration or manifestation of the will of him that commandeth, by voice, writing, or some other sufficient argument of the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only those to whom the declaration can be made (who have means to take notice of it) are bound; the will of the Sovereign is the source of civil law; subordinate judges should regard the reason which moved their Sovereign to make such law so their sentence may accord to it (otherwise their sentence is their own and unjust).

rubrics_metrics.name: Law Must Be Made Known To Be Law
rubrics_metrics.description: From this, that the Law is a Command ... we may understand, that the Command of the Common-wealth, is Law only to those, that have means to take notice of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over natural fools, children, or mad-men there is no Law; those deprived (by accident not their fault) of means to take notice of a particular law are excused; law is not properly law to him. Therefore consider what arguments and signs are sufficient for knowledge of what is the law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unwritten Universal Laws Are Laws of Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: If it be a Law that obliges all the Subjects without exception, and is not written, nor otherwise published ... it is a Law of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such laws are known not by others' words but by each person's own reason and need no publishing or proclamation; example summarized by 'Do not that to another, which thou thinkest unreasonable to be done by another to thyself.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Unwritten Particular Laws May Also Be Natural
rubrics_metrics.description: If it be a Law that obliges only some condition of men, or one particular man and be not written, nor published by word, then also it is a Law of Nature; and known by the same arguments, and signs, that distinguish those in such a condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g. public ministers without written instructions must take the dictates of reason for guidance (judge to apply equity; ambassador to act for sovereign's interest). All such instructions of natural reason fall under 'Fidelity', a branch of natural justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law Requires Manifest Signs of Sovereign Authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Nor is it enough the Law be written, and published; but also that there be manifest signs, that it proceedeth from the will of the Soveraign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private men may publish spurious laws; verification requires public registers, public counsels, public ministers, and public seals by which laws are sufficiently verified; verification (testimony/record) is distinct from authorization (authority resides only in the sovereign's command).

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification by Subordinate Judge
rubrics_metrics.description: If ... a question of injury, depending on the Law of Nature ... the Sentence of the Judge, that by Commission hath Authority to take cognisance of such causes, is a sufficient Verification of the Law of Nature in that individuall case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though lawyers' advice is useful, it is the judge who must tell men what is law upon hearing controversy; the judge's sentence verifies but does not originate authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to Inform Oneself of Written Law
rubrics_metrics.description: When the question is of injury, or crime, upon a written Law; every man by recourse to the Registers ... may (if he will) be sufficiently enformed, before he doe such injury, or commit the crime, whether it be an injury, or not: Nay he ought to doe so: for when a man doubts ... the doing is unlawful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person who complains before consulting applicable written law acts unjustly and reveals inclination to vex rather than to seek right; citizens are obliged to use due diligence to learn written laws affecting their actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority Verification for Public Officers
rubrics_metrics.description: If the question be of Obedience to a publique Officer; To have seen his Commission, with the Publique Seale, and heard it read; or to have had the means to be informed of it, is a sufficient Verification of his Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every man is obliged to do his best endeavour to inform himself of all written laws and commissions that may concern his future actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of the Law Depends on Sovereign Power
rubrics_metrics.description: The Interpretation of all Lawes dependeth on the Authority Soveraign; and the Interpreters can be none but those, which the Soveraign ... shall appoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without an interpreter authorized by the sovereign, interpreters may make law contrary to the sovereign's meaning; authentic interpretation (the sense of the legislator) resides in the sovereign and those he authorizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: All Laws Need Interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: All Laws, written, and unwritten, have need of Interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unwritten law of nature is especially obscure due to passions and partiality; written laws, whether short or long, are ambiguous and require understanding of the final causes for which the law was made — knowledge which lies with the legislator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writers' Authority Does Not Constitute Law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authenticall Interpretation Of Law Is Not That Of Writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral philosophy or authors' opinions, however true, are not law without the authority of the commonwealth; commentaries need other commentaries and cannot substitute for sovereign authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge's Sentence as Authentic Interpretation in Particular Cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Interpreter Of The Law Is The Judge Giving Sentence Vivâ Voce In Every Particular Case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The judge applies law to the present case; his sentence is authentique for the parties pleading because given by authority of the sovereign, thereby becoming the sovereign's sentence for that time to the parties involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial Sentences Do Not Bind Future Judges in Perpetuity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sentence Of A Judge, Does Not Bind Him, Or Another Judge To Give Like Sentence In Like Cases Ever After.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges subordinate or sovereign may err and later give contrary sentence; no man's error becomes law perpetually; precedent cannot make a law contrary to natural equity; wrong sentences do not bind succeeding judges as law in matters of natural law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction Between Letter and Intention (Sentence) of the Law
rubrics_metrics.description: In written Lawes, men use to make a difference between the Letter, and the Sentence of the Law ... the letter (bare words) may be ambiguous; there is only one sense of the Law, the intention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the letter does not authorise a reasonable sentence, judge should supply it with the Law of Nature or respit judgement until more authority is had; the literal application must not produce injustice (e.g., avoid condemning the innocent by literal reading).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge's Required Qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: The things that make a good Judge, or good Interpreter of the Lawes, are, first A Right Understanding of that principall Law of Nature called Equity ... Secondly, Contempt Of Unnecessary Riches, and Preferments. Thirdly, To Be Able In Judgement To Devest Himselfe Of All Feare, Anger, Hatred, Love, And Compassion. Fourthly ... Patience To Heare; Diligent Attention In Hearing; And Memory To Retain, Digest And Apply What He Hath Heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge need not be same as advocate or scholar of laws; must take notice of facts only from witnesses and of law only from statutes/constitutions alleged in pleading or declared by authorized persons; personal passions and corruption must be absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisions of Law (classificatory standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws may be divided variously (e.g., edicts of prince, decrees of people, senatus consulta, edicts of praetors, responsa prudentum, unwritten customs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different historical forms correspond to modern analogues (proclamations, acts of parliament, orders of commons, acts of council, judicial edicts, reports/opinions of lawyers, customary law). This is a taxonomy useful for identifying sources and forms of positive law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural vs Positive Law
rubrics_metrics.description: Another division of Laws is into Naturall and Positive. Naturall are those which have been Laws from all Eternity ... Positive are those which ... have been made Laws by the Will of those that have had the Soveraign Power over others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural laws (moral virtues like justice) do not require promulgation; positive laws derive from sovereign will and may be written or otherwise declared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdivision of Positive Laws (human/divine; distributive/penal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of Positive Lawes some are Humane, some Divine; And of Humane positive lawes, some are Distributive, some Penal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributive laws determine subjects' rights and speak to all; penal laws declare penalties for violators and speak to ministers appointed for execution; penal laws are usually written with distributive laws and sometimes called judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divine Positive Law and Public Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Divine Positive Laws ... are those, which being the Commandements of God ... are declared for such, by those whom God hath authorised to declare them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without supernatural revelation to each subject, men are bound to obey divine positive law declared by the commonwealth so long as it is not contrary to natural law; private revelations cannot supersede public declaration; obedience is a duty arising from subjects' submission and covenant to their sovereign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental Laws vs Non-Fundamental
rubrics_metrics.description: A Fundamentall Law in every Common-wealth is that, which being taken away, the Common-wealth faileth, and is utterly dissolved ... Not Fundamentall is that the abrogating whereof, draweth not with it the dissolution of the Common-Wealth; such as are the Lawes Concerning Controversies between subject and subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental laws include powers of war and peace, judicature, election of officers, and doing what sovereign thinks necessary for public good; this distinction helps prioritize which laws sustain the polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference Between Law and Right
rubrics_metrics.description: Right is Liberty ... Civill Law is an Obligation; and takes from us the Liberty which the Law of Nature gave us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lex and Jus differ as Obligation and Liberty; civil law removes certain natural liberties to enable protection and order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference Between Law and Charter
rubrics_metrics.description: Likewise Lawes and Charters are taken promiscuously for the same thing. Yet Charters are Donations of the Soveraign; and not Lawes, but exemptions from Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrase of a Law is 'Jubeo, Injungo' (I command); phrase of a Charter is 'Dedi, Concessi' (I have given). A charter grants liberty only to particular persons or groups and does not bind the entire commonwealth as a law does.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Sin vs Crime
rubrics_metrics.description: A Sinne, is not onely a Transgression of a Law, but also any Contempt of the Legislator ... A Crime, is a sinne, consisting in the Committing (by Deed, or Word) of that which the Law forbiddeth, or the Omission of what it hath commanded. So that every Crime is a sinne; but not every sinne a Crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intentions alone (first motions of the mind) may be sins in a theological sense but not humanly prosecutable unless manifested; crime presupposes civil law and the capacity for human accusation and judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where No Civil Law Exists, No Crime
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Law ceaseth, Sinne ceaseth ... the Civill Law ceasing, Crimes cease: for there being no other Law remaining, but that of Nature, there is no place for Accusation;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In absence of civil law or sovereign power subjects revert to self-preservation and conscience; when sovereign power ceases, crime as a category ceases except where individuals contributed to removal of that power (which was itself a crime).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ignorance of Law of Nature Excuseth No Man
rubrics_metrics.description: The source of every Crime, is some defect of the Understanding; or some errour in Reasoning, or some sudden force of the Passions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although ignorance of positive law may excuse when deprived by accident of means to know it, ignorance of the Law of Nature does not excuse; violations of natural law remain morally blameworthy.
